newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares bounce off 25-mth lows at close.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares bounce off 25-mth lows at close.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) bounced back from a 25-month low at Tuesday's close but dealers said the market looked poised for further falls soon.
The STII settled at 2,032.97 points, down 1.67, and above an intraday low of 2,027.11 reached late afternoon.
Dealers said the index had been dragged lower by foreign fund selling and a drop in the nearby Malaysian stock market.
"Technical support has already been broken and people are talking about 1,900, if support at 2,000 goes," said a dealer.
"But we're not expecting a meltdown," said another dealer.
He said one crumb of comfort was the fact that market volume had been a relatively light 160 million shares, indicating widespread liquidation had not occurred.
Shares in state shipping company Neptune Orient Lines, which resumed trading on Tuesday after announcing a takeover bid for U.S.-based carrier APL, were last up six cents at S$1.26.

Of the 30 STI component stocks, drinks firm Fraser & Neave fell 30 cents to Singapore $10.70 while food group Cerebos lost 20 cents to S$8.90. Multi-media firm Creative gained most, up S$1.00 to S$17.70 on rumours of a broker recommendation.
